clue.text: One unable to cope with everyday life in bygone capital, we hear

definitions.text: One unable to cope with everyday life

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the spelling of the words before it may change

blocks.note: Seoul, the South Korean capital, gone missing: a capital now lost

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the past, in a city of yesteryear, struggles with ordinary life.
explanation.walkthrough: Seoul and soul are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost soul is an idiom for a person who seems helpless and adrift in the world.

clue.text: TT really rousing, recently

indicators.note: rousing stirs things up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man TT motorcycle races have been truly thrilling of late.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Latterly is a synonym for lately, in the recent period of time.

clue.text: Wrecking boats at sea over long period of time

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
an age is a long period

explanation.surface: Boats are wrecked at sea over a long stretch of years.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is the deliberate wrecking of something, so the noun stands for the act of wrecking.

clue.text: Energy shown by second eleven?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a cricket or football side has eleven players

explanation.surface: Asks whether a club's reserve side shows much vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' looks like a reserve side, but splits into the abbreviation for second and a word for an eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam means drive or vigour, as in running out of steam.

clue.text: Unorthodox place for nuns in harmony by a lake

indicators.note: in puts one thing inside another, so the place for nuns sits within the word for harmony

blocks.note: union is harmony or agreement
nuns live in a convent
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A convent beside a lake where nuns live harmoniously is an unusual setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place for nuns in harmony' reads as nuns living in harmony, but 'in' is the instruction to put one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional is a synonym for unorthodox, not following accepted norms.

clue.text: A grand on top

blocks.note: taken as written
swell is an old-fashioned word for splendid or grand

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds extra, perhaps, on top of what was agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A grand' looks like a thousand pounds; here grand is the adjective, swell.
explanation.definitionFit: On top, meaning in addition, is a synonym for the phrase as well.

clue.text: Small Buddhist priest featured in article about a Spanish city

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so the priest sits within the article

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
an is the indefinite article
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest
ca is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A short Buddhist monk is featured in a piece written about a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the subject of the article, but it is the Latin abbreviation ca (circa) attached at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamanca is a university city in western Spain, in the region of Castile and León.

clue.text: Fur in emergency room belonging to me

blocks.note: ER is the abbreviation for emergency room
mine means belonging to me

explanation.surface: Someone claims a fur coat left in the hospital's emergency room as theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat, used to trim robes.

clue.text: Bet placed by servant, a member of the congregation

blocks.note: to lay a bet is to place it
a manservant, or man, is a servant

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's wager was placed by his butler.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman is a non-clergy member of a church, someone among the congregation rather than the clergy.

clue.text: A heart broken by candid leader of line-up, popular soul singer

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters reassemble differently
the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
frank means candid
the first letter of line-up
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A soul singer leading a group has her heart broken by honest words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular soul singer' reads as one phrase, but popular is the last piece of wordplay, leaving 'soul singer' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aretha Franklin was the American vocalist known as the Queen of Soul.

clue.text: Story about British item of furniture

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story wraps round the letter for British

blocks.note: a tale is a story
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A tale about a piece of British furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is a common piece of furniture with a flat top on legs.

clue.text: Fruit brought into Northants town? Good heavens!

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside, so the fruit goes within the town

blocks.note: Corby is a town in Northamptonshire, an English county
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at fruit being imported into a Northamptonshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor blimey is a British exclamation of surprise, from 'God blind me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cor blimey is a Cockney exclamation of astonishment, equivalent to good heavens.

clue.text: I'm tense at shabby café

indicators.note: shabby means rundown and disordered, so the letters are disarranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone feels nervous sitting in a rundown café.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or café, a word familiar from the First World War.

clue.text: Soldier, one with a fixation

blocks.note: a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier who has an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: A mania is an obsessive enthusiasm or craze, a synonym for a fixation.

clue.text: Greed in male unfortunately leads to deception

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's avarice regrettably ends in trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Legerdemain is sleight of hand, and by extension any trickery or deceit.

clue.text: Practical articles reproduced about electric current

indicators.note: reproduced here means made over again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the symbol for current

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Practical articles about electricity are reprinted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ARTICLES are rearranged around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means sensible and practical, having a grasp of what is achievable.

clue.text: As a member of the clergy, I must be found in cathedral

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the letter goes within the cathedral word

blocks.note: a minster is a large church or cathedral, such as York Minster
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman says he is required to be present in the cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a clergyman, especially in Protestant churches.

clue.text: One new flavour available

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new
to season food is to flavour it

explanation.surface: A new flavour has come out.
explanation.walkthrough: Flavour is read as a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is in season is readily available at that time of year.

clue.text: Change involving centigrade results in an argument

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the word for change encloses the letter for centigrade

blocks.note: an alteration is a change
C is the abbreviation for centigrade

explanation.surface: Adjusting the thermostat's centigrade setting causes a row.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or dispute.

clue.text: Go along with company representative, extremely lazy

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative
the first and last letters of lazy

explanation.surface: Someone goes along with a very idle company rep.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply is to act in accordance with a request, synonymous with going along with it.

clue.text: Runs onto a jetty producing sword

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written
a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: Someone dashes onto a jetty, brandishing a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a thin, light sword used for thrusting.

clue.text: In textbook, a picture showing a ruminant

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning them

blocks.note: letters running across textbook, a and picture

explanation.surface: A textbook has an illustration of a cud-chewing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a giraffe relative from the Congo, and like all giraffids it chews the cud.

clue.text: Oscar and I phone eccentric, the Parisian wine connoisseur

indicators.note: eccentric means odd and off-centre, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone telephones Oscar, an odd French wine expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a lover and connoisseur of wines, from the Greek for wine-loving.

clue.text: Court plaster in shop at chateau

indicators.note: in says the answer is contained within the following words

blocks.note: letters running across shop, at and chateau

explanation.surface: A shop at a French chateau sells sticking plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Court plaster is a historic sticking plaster, once also used for beauty spots worn at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a small piece of material stuck over a wound or worn as a beauty spot, as court plaster was.

clue.text: Colouring round object in game

blocks.note: paint is colouring
a ball is round

explanation.surface: Someone colours a ball used in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a combat game in which players shoot pellets of dye at each other.

clue.text: Emperor beginning to try on new suit

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
new suggests a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the first letter of try
taken as written

explanation.surface: An emperor starts trying on a new suit, like the fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was Roman emperor from AD 79 to 81.

clue.text: King's jester in charge in royal house

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the abbreviation goes within the royal house

blocks.note: York was an English royal house
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: The king's fool is put in charge in the royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorick is the dead jester of the Danish king whose skull Hamlet holds.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet, Yorick was the late jester to the king of Denmark.

clue.text: Fleeing astride galloping hunter

indicators.note: galloping implies vigorous motion, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: a rider astride a horse is on it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider escapes sitting on a galloping hunter, a horse bred for hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: On the run is an idiom for escaping or fleeing from pursuit.
